findings.symbol: src/spine/units.py::Clock.convert -- ITEM 1, the float division derive refuses by name
findings.detail: CONFIRMED, WIDENED, AND REPAIRED. The body was `return to(int(self.n / per))` -- float division -- while the closing comment of src/spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_backwards refuses exactly that: 'Integer `//` and not `int(n / k)`: float division loses exactness above 2**53 and a backward count is unbounded.' WHAT convert IS FOR: it is the DECLARED cross-kind path, the rule quoted by units.py's own docstring and by tests/test_ownership.py::check_o11_no_unnamed_clock_arithmetic. WHO CALLS IT: exactly TWO sites in the whole repository, `grep -rn '\.convert(' --include=*.py .` -> src/spine/derive.py:236 (flush_period) and src/spine/derive.py:292 (flush_period_windows), plus the mention in units.py's own docstring. Nothing else in src/, tests/, tools/ or the frozen old tree calls it. So it is NOT dead code -- two of derive's five clock conversions were performing in float the operation derive's other three refuse by name, precisely BECAUSE they delegate here instead of dividing themselves. IS FLOAT EVER THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR A CLOCK QUANTITY: no, and the reason is stronger than lost precision. A clock is a count of events and the rate is exactly known, so the answer is an exact rational truncated to an integer. Measured on the tree before the repair: flush_period(Steps(2**53+1), 1) -> 9007199254740992 against an exact 9007199254740993; flush_period(Steps(10**17+1), 3) -> 33333333333333332 against an exact 33333333333333333; AND -- the case the previous round did not find -- flush_period(Steps(2**53+3), 2) -> 4503599627370498 against an exact 4503599627370497, ONE FLUSH LARGER than the true period. Float does not only lose digits, it can round UP, and a period that rounds up FIRES LATE, which is the direction both callers' docstrings name as the one they refuse to bias toward ('A period that truncates fires marginally EARLY; a period that rounds up fires late'). That makes it a false guarantee in a docstring, not only an inexactness. THE REPAIR REFUSES IT THE WAY derive DOES WITHOUT NARROWING THE RATE: `per` is documented as possibly fractional (`Flushes(250).convert(Steps, per=1/batch_w)`), so `//` alone cannot serve; the body is now `to(int(Fraction(self.n, 1) / Fraction(per)))`, exact at every magnitude and for every rate, and int() on a Fraction TRUNCATES TOWARD ZERO -- the rounding both callers already attribute to this method, preserved at every input including negatives. A `per` Fraction cannot take (nan, inf -- both pass the `per <= 0` test today) now raises UnitError instead of raising ValueError out of int() or silently answering 0. The docstring records who calls it, the measurement, why Fraction and not `//`, and the one thing Fraction does NOT fix (a float `per` like 1/3 is already inexact when it arrives; pass Fraction(1, 3)). NO LIVE NUMBER MOVES -- live cadences are in the tens of thousands -- and that is stated in the docstring rather than used as a reason not to fix it.
findings.repro: BEFORE (git stash or HEAD): python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'src');from spine import derive;from spine.units import Steps;print(int(derive.flush_period(Steps(2**53+1),1)), int(derive.flush_period(Steps(2**53+3),2)), int(derive.flush_period(Steps(10**17+1),3)))" ;; 9007199254740992 4503599627370498 33333333333333332, against exact 9007199254740993 4503599627370497 33333333333333333. AFTER: the same three ;; 9007199254740993 4503599627370497 33333333333333333, all exact. NEIGHBOURS UNMOVED: flush_period(Steps(20000),16) ;; 1250 flushes; flush_period(Steps(8),16) ;; 1 flushes; flush_period(Steps(0),4) ;; 1 flushes; flush_period_windows(Windows(2000),16) ;; 125 flushes; Flushes(250).convert(Steps,per=1/16) ;; 4000 steps; Steps(-5).convert(Flushes,per=4) ;; -1 flushes (truncation preserved; floor would be -2). REFUSALS: per=nan and per=inf ;; UnitError 'convert() rate must have an exact value' (before the repair: nan raised ValueError from int(), inf answered 0 flushes). CALL SITES: grep -rn '\.convert(' --include=*.py . ;; src/spine/derive.py:236, src/spine/derive.py:292, and the docstring line in units.py. Suite after: 5 files green except the pre-existing O13 finding on src/eval/api.py.

findings.symbol: src/spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_backwards -- ITEM 2, the false clause in the UnitError message
findings.detail: CONFIRMED FALSE AND REPLACED WITH WHAT IS TRUE. The message ended: 'This was caught until 2026-09-04 only as a side effect of `//` flooring a partial step up into a whole one, WHICH MISSED EVERY DEFICIT SMALLER THAN ACCUM; it is checked here now.' Flooring missed NOTHING: floor(n/k) <= -1 for every n < 0 and k >= 1, so under floor every negative delta came back non-zero and opt/api.py::counters' `due != taken` fired. The deficits smaller than accum were missed by TRUNCATION -- the same day's earlier rounding repair -- which is what the function's own docstring says twelve lines above, so the file held two statements about one mechanism and the one a run would PRINT was the wrong one. Enumerated, not argued: for k in (1,2,4,8) x n in (-1,-2,-3,-4,-5,-8,-9), floor gives 0 in zero of the 28 cases; truncation gives 0 in nine of them, exactly the (n,k) pairs with |n| < k. THE REPLACEMENT says what floor actually did, why that detection was weak (it was a COMPARISON, so a resume that lost accum backward passes AND one optimizer step gave due == taken and cancelled it -- at accum=4, due=Steps(-1) against taken=Steps(-1)), that truncation then removed even that, and that the refusal is now on the count itself at every magnitude. SECOND, IN THE SAME FUNCTION AND ALSO FIXED: the docstring said 'The message below names the two counter keys instead' while the message names FOUR (opt.ckpt.backward_at_load, opt.ckpt.step_at_load, opt.backward, opt.step). It now says FOUR and lists them. THE FALSE CLAUSE IS QUEUED TO TRAVEL into src/opt/api.py -- x_spine's unfinished proposes it verbatim -- and the corrected wording is in this report's unfinished so it does not.
findings.repro: python3 -c "...; derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(-3), 4)" ;; the message now reads '... Until 2026-09-04 this was caught only as a SIDE EFFECT of `//` flooring: floor(n/k) is at most -1 for every n < 0, so no deficit came back as zero and opt/api.py::counters raised on the comparison. Being a comparison is what made it weak -- a resume that lost accum backward passes AND one optimizer step gave due == taken and cancelled it -- and the same-day repair from flooring to TRUNCATION then removed even that, answering Steps(0) for every deficit smaller than accum. It is checked here now, on the count itself, at every magnitude.' THE ARITHMETIC: python3 -c "rows=[(n,k,n//k,int(n/k)) for k in (1,2,4,8) for n in (-1,-2,-3,-4,-5,-8,-9)]; print(any(r[2]==0 for r in rows), [(r[0],r[1]) for r in rows if r[3]==0])" ;; False, [(-1,2),(-1,4),(-2,4),(-3,4),(-1,8),(-2,8),(-3,8),(-4,8),(-5,8)] -- floor never zero, truncation zero exactly when |n| < k. grep -n 'names the two counter keys' src/spine/derive.py ;; no match (now 'names the FOUR counter keys').
